title: Ending an Authorization Before Its Expiration Date (Utilization Management Program)
content:
Under the Utilization Management Program an authorization ends early only when one of three things happens:

1. plan coverage ends — recorded as *coverage ended*, while the package ends approvals with coverage;
2. a renewal replaces it — recorded as *replaced by renewal*;
3. the prescriber asks to end it because therapy stopped — recorded as *prescriber request*.

A member's request alone never ends it.

An authorization may be ended only once, by naming the granted authorization it ends. The authorization's own history in the system records is what shows whether it has already been ended.

On a COBRA reinstatement, approvals ended for *coverage ended* resume through their original expiration date. When the sponsor changes review package, approvals in force carry over while the package carries approvals over on a package change.

## Who can bring an early end about

| Requested by or arising from | Ends the authorization early |
|---|---|
| End of plan coverage | Yes (coverage ended) |
| A renewal that replaces it | Yes (replaced by renewal) |
| The prescriber, because therapy stopped | Yes (prescriber request) |
| The member alone | No |

### Hypothetical cases

- A member asks to cancel an approval they no longer want; without a prescriber request because therapy stopped, the approval stays in force.
- An approval running to 30 November was ended on 30 June because plan coverage ended; the member's coverage is restored by COBRA reinstatement, and the approval resumes through 30 November.
- An authorization already ended for *replaced by renewal* is not ended a second time.
